Generating a Mock Galaxy Catalog¶

Selection Methods¶

There are two ways to select your galaxy sample in RAFIKI-CGM.

Ranges (selection.method: ranges)

Selects all galaxies within the simulation that fall within specified galaxy property ranges. Currently cuts can be made by stellar mass, halo mass, specific star formation rate, and/or whether the galaxy is central in its halo. With this selection, sample size is set by how many galaxies in a given simulation box match the properties you choose. If no galaxies fit the criteria, the pipeline won’t run.

Matching (selection.method: matching)

Resamples the simulation to match the stellar or halo mass distribution of a comparison catalog (i.e. an observational sample). Galaxies are binned and resampled with weights corresponding to the representation of their mass bin in the comparison distribution.

Key parameters:

  • bins - mass bin edges used for matching distributions

  • n_sample - number of galaxies to resample (the final stack will be three times this value, one per projection direction)

  • match_property - property to match on (currently limited to stellar_mass or halo_mass)

Note

Any cuts set in selection.property_ranges will also be applied before matching. This allows for cominations, for example applying a halo mass cut to exclude clusters before matching an observed stellar mass distribution

Warning

Larger n_sample values will more closely match the comparison catalog, but the runtime will increase accordingly. See the images below that show the difference in distribution matching between N=400 (~20 minute runtime) and N=1000 (~1 hour runtime).

Assigning Redshifts¶

Once galaxies are selected, they are each assigned a redshift for mock observation. There are three ways to do this in RAFIKI-CGM.

Fixed (selection.redshift_sampling: fixed)

Places every galaxy at a fixed redshift (suggested to be the redshift of snapshot)

Key parameters:

  • selection.redshift_sampling.fixed_z - redshift

Matching Redshift Distribution (selection.redshift_sampling: redshift)

Randomly selects and assigns redshifts from a user-provided comparison catalog (i.e. an observational sample).

Key parameters:

  • selection.redshift_sampling.observational_catalog - Path to catalog containing redshift distribution you wish to resample from

  • selection.redshift_sampling.z_column - Column corresponding to the redshift data in the linked file

Matching Redshift Distribution within Mass Bins (selection.redshift_sampling: mass_redshift)

Randomly selects and assigns redshifts from a user-provided comparison catalog after binning by stellar mass. This methodology can be used to account for baises in the sampling.

Key parameters:

  • selection.redshift_sampling.observational_catalog - Path to catalog containing redshift distribution you wish to resample from

  • selection.redshift_sampling.z_column - Column corresponding to the redshift data in the linked file

  • selection.redshift_sampling.mass_column - Column corresponding to the stellar mass data in the linked file

  • selection.redshift_sampling.mass_bins - Mass bin edges used for matching distribution

It is worth noting that the ways in which galaxy sample redshifts are incorporated are very different in the tSZ and X-ray pipelines. In the X-ray pipeline, the redshift is taken into account when generating photons both in terms of photon energies changing and the distance of the observation impacting psf. The tSZ data, the redshift is only used to determine the scale of the convolving beam as the actual Compton-y parameter is independent of redshift.
